citation.authors: Benedict C, Vogel H, Jonas W, Woting A, Blaut M, Schürmann A, Cedernaes J
citation.title: Gut microbiota and glucometabolic alterations in response to recurrent partial sleep deprivation in normal-weight young individuals

reported.what: fasting insulin after two nights of partial sleep deprivation (PSD) vs normal sleep (NS), n=9, mean ± SEM, morning of the OGTT day

location.where: Results, 'Effects of partial sleep deprivation on glucometabolic parameters', paragraph 1
location.quote: fasting insulin values were 34% higher following PSD than after NS (4.26 ± 0.48 vs. 3.17 ± 0.35 μU/mL, P = 0.006, one-sided)

reported.what: fasting plasma glucose after two nights of PSD vs NS, n=9, mean ± SEM

location.where: Results, 'Effects of partial sleep deprivation on glucometabolic parameters', paragraph 1
location.quote: glucose values were not significantly different at baseline (5.27 ± 0.07 vs. 5.12 ± 0.10 mmol/L; P = 0.14, one-sided)

reported.what: Matsuda index (OGTT, 75 g) after two nights of PSD vs NS, n=9, mean ± SEM; a derived index

location.where: Results, 'Effects of partial sleep deprivation on glucometabolic parameters', paragraph 1
location.quote: the Matsuda index (8.0 ± 0.90 vs. 10.2 ± 0.78, P = 0.017, one-sided

reported.what: HOMA-IR in the fasting state after PSD vs NS, n=9, mean ± SEM; a derived index

location.where: Results, 'Effects of partial sleep deprivation on glucometabolic parameters', paragraph 1
location.quote: as assessed by the HOMA-IR index in the fasting state on the third day (1.01 ± 0.12 vs. 0.72 ± 0.08, P = 0.014, one-sided; Figure 3)

detail: Every glucose and insulin value is measured after two nights of sleep restriction (or normal sleep) and after a day of meals that the paper gives only as energy (33% of the estimated daily calorie requirement each, with no grams of carbohydrate, fat or protein), so a multi-day arm cannot be written without grams the paper does not print; the OGTT curves are in Figure 3 only.
